brief.topic: The Note Inside an Empty Space

s01: An empty bottle has a note hidden in its air.
This gentle tone represents one possible resonance.
Listen before we change the space inside.
The air near the neck moves like a small mass.
The air in the body compresses and pushes back.
Together, they behave rather like a spring and a weight.
Keep the neck the same, and add water below it.
The remaining air is harder to compress by the same amount.
When only a quarter of the air volume remains, the resonance frequency doubles.
Here, two hundred and twenty vibrations per second become four hundred and forty.
These are synthesized tones, not recordings of the bottle.
Hear the larger space, then the smaller one.
The rule is an inverse square root: frequency grows as air volume shrinks.
It assumes small vibrations and a bottle much smaller than the sound wavelength.
Real neck shape and losses matter too.
A little empty space can have a voice of its own.

scenes.narration:
An empty bottle has a note hidden in its air. This gentle tone represents one possible resonance. Listen before we change the space inside.

The air near the neck moves like a small mass. The air in the body compresses and pushes back. Together, they behave rather like a spring and a weight.

Keep the neck the same, and add water below it. The remaining air is harder to compress by the same amount. When only a quarter of the air volume remains, the resonance frequency doubles.

Here, two hundred and twenty vibrations per second become four hundred and forty. These are synthesized tones, not recordings of the bottle. Hear the larger space, then the smaller one.

The rule is an inverse square root: frequency grows as air volume shrinks. It assumes small vibrations and a bottle much smaller than the sound wavelength. Real neck shape and losses matter too. A little empty space can have a voice of its own.
